name: Gilt market
summary: Gilt yields rise after the Bank of England's first hike since 2023 on 5 Nov
state: Gilt yields rose on 5 Nov after the Bank of England raised Bank Rate to 4%, its first rise in three years, with two-year gilts most affected (Euronext). The 10-year yield was near 5.2% in early November, below its mid-October multi-year high near 5.4% (Trading Economics). No weak auction or BoE intervention has been reported.
for_you: Higher gilt yields feed through to fixed mortgage pricing and annuity rates.
rubric_hit: 30y at multi-decade highs = Watch; no BoE intervention

sources.title: Euronext — Bank of England delivers first rate hike in three years, gilt yields rise

why: Gilt yields set UK mortgage rates and the government's borrowing costs; the 2022 LDI crisis showed how fast it can break.
drivers: Fiscal credibility, BoE policy, inflation, global bond moves, pension-fund flows.

rubric.alert: BoE intervention, or 10y moved > 75bp in a month.
rubric.watch: 30y gilt at multi-decade highs, or 10y moved 40–75bp in a month, or a weak auction.
rubric.normal: 10y gilt moved < 40bp in a month and auctions orderly.
